title: NVIDIA’s AI-Powerhouse “DGX Station” Breaks Out Of Linux, Cramming 748 GB Of Memory And 20 PFLOPs Into A Windows Workstation
key_facts: Nvidia has announced a Windows version of its DGX Station, which until now ran only on Linux; enterprise developers had to keep two environments.
The DGX Station has a single GB300 'Blackwell Ultra' GPU with 252 GB of HBM3e memory, plus a 72-core Grace CPU with 496 GB of LPDDR5X, for 748 GB in total.
Wccftech cites 20 PFLOPs of compute, 900 GB/s CPU-GPU link bandwidth, an 800 Gb/s networking card and a 1600W TDP.
Nvidia plans a release in Q4 2026 but has not shared an exact date.
Wccftech puts the price at around $100,000 and says AMD's Threadripper Halo Station, due in 2027, should be priced similarly.
The article says the figures are on paper and real-world AI results will differ.
quote_evidence: The system was initially compatible with Linux distros, but today, the company has announced it's bringing DGX Station for Windows.
While the Halo Station is primed for a 2027 release, NVIDIA has not shared an exact date for the DGX Station for Windows, but they plan to release it in Q4 of this year.
These are only on paper; the real-world advantages within AI will be a whole different thing to talk about.
why_it_matters_hint: Windows-based developers can use a large AI workstation without moving to Linux; Nvidia targets enterprise teams.
